text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Canada asked to hold Pol Pot in jail: U.S. wants international tribunal to put ex-Khmer Rouge leader on trial for crimes against humanity.
- RRSP ceiling may be raised, Martin says: Tax relief and pension reform top Finance Minister's wish list.
- Canada wins support for land-mine stand: Communique reveals summit changes.
- Former leader oversaw end of Big Blue Machine dynasty.
- Canada fails to get salmon talks restarted: Federal officials leave summit frustrated by U.S. refusal to submit to arbitration in fish dispute.
- Copps to screen Cineplex talks: Heritage Minister aims to promote Canadian films in potential merger with Sony unit.
- Merchant banking a growing force: More institutions hop on bandwagon.
- No winners seen in beer war: Analysts say fight for Ontario could hurt big, small brewers.
- Experts growing more bearish about Canadian stocks, bonds.
- Landmark tobacco deal: U.S. tobacco industry to pay US$368.5 billion over 25 years for cost of smoking related illness - a deal that is being watched closely in Canada.
- Chalk River strike turns off supply of medical isotopes.
